blocks.content: A Joint State Public Service Commission is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, not a constitutional body.

items: JSPSC is a statutory body, unlike UPSC and SPSC which are constitutional bodies.
Despite serving state needs, JSPSC members are appointed and removed by the President, not the Governor.
JSPSC submits its annual report to the respective State Governors, who then present it to the State Legislatures.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution provides for the establishment of a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) for two or more states upon agreement.
Unlike UPSC and SPSC, a JSPSC is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament rather than directly by the Constitution.
The Chairman and members of a JSPSC are appointed by the President of India.
Members hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
A JSPSC presents its annual performance report to the Governors of the participating states, who lay it before their respective state legislatures.
